lead.headline: OVER 150 FALL ILL AFTER EATING PANI PURI IN SIDDHARTHNAGAR
lead.deck: Children are among those being treated; doctors are waiting for test results to establish what caused the suspected outbreak
paragraphs: More than 150 people, including children, reportedly fell ill after eating pani puri from a roadside vendor in Siddharthnagar district, Uttar Pradesh. Several children were admitted to hospital with vomiting and other symptoms.
An emergency duty doctor said around 30 to 32 children had been brought in for treatment. Doctors suspect contaminated water or spoiled food, but the cause has not been confirmed.
Patients are receiving care as authorities await test reports and investigate the source of the suspected foodborne outbreak.

image.alt: Representative pani puri image accompanying the report on the Siddharthnagar illness outbreak
image.caption: Representative image. Photo: Pixabay / India Today

sidebarStory.headline: FOUR KILLED IN THREE SEPARATE BENGALURU ROAD CRASHES
sidebarStory.subhead: The fatal crashes occurred between Friday evening and Saturday morning in Electronics City, HSR Layout and KR Puram
paragraphs: Four people died in three separate road accidents in Bengaluru. Two people on a motorcycle were killed in a hit-and-run on the Bommasandra flyover; police are reviewing CCTV footage to identify the vehicle. Two other motorcyclists died in separate crashes.

groups.ariaLabel: Bengaluru traffic, connectivity, and city life news

stories.headline: HEBBAL FLYOVER TO STAY OPEN DURING 18-MONTH CORRIDOR WORK
paragraphs: The BDA says Hebbal Flyover and Ballari Road will not be fully closed during construction of the elevated corridor toward Mehkri Circle. One lane in each direction may be occupied by barricades, while two lanes and the service road are expected to remain open; goods vehicles will face restrictions under traffic police advisories.

stories.headline: KARNATAKA CLEARS EXTRA ₹1,118.5 CRORE FOR 134-KM OUTER ROAD
paragraphs: The Karnataka Cabinet approved an additional ₹1,118.5 crore for the 134-km Bengaluru Peripheral Road, connecting Anekal, Sarjapur, Varthur and Nelamangala. The project also includes an elevated stretch at Varthur and railway crossing flyovers; the report gave no revised completion date.

stories.headline: RESIDENTS REOPEN RESTORED AANE PARK AFTER TWO DECADES
paragraphs: Residents and volunteers have restored Malleswaram’s long-neglected Aane Park, including its elephant slide and children’s play area. A mural celebrating the neighbourhood’s history is another feature of the community-led revival, carried out with the Horticulture Department.

image.alt: The restored elephant-themed Aane Park in Malleswaram
image.caption: The restored elephant park in Malleswaram. Photo: The New Indian Express

groups.ariaLabel: India public safety, rail, and health news

stories.headline: MISSING CONSTABLE FOUND DEAD IN RIVER; FOUR ARRESTED
paragraphs: Bihar Police constable Dhaneshwar Kumar’s body was recovered from the Dardha River two days after he went missing during a drug and arms investigation in Jehanabad. Police said questioning indicated he was assaulted and thrown into the river; four people have been arrested as the investigation continues.

stories.headline: NEW PRICE CAPS ON 137 ANTI-CANCER DRUGS TAKE EFFECT TODAY
paragraphs: Revised prices for 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines take effect on November 9 after the government capped trade margins. The Department of Pharmaceuticals estimates annual consumer savings of ₹3,502 crore; retailers, hospitals and drug controllers are to implement and monitor the revised prices.

stories.headline: STONE SHATTERS WINDOW ON SABARMATI–VERAVAL VANDE BHARAT
paragraphs: A stone-pelting incident in Amreli district shattered a window on the Sabarmati–Veraval Vande Bharat Express on Diwali morning. The report called it the third such incident involving a Vande Bharat train in Gujarat in four months.

stories.headline: BJP AND CONGRESS TRADE CLAIMS OVER CREDIT FOR NAMMA METRO
paragraphs: Ahead of the Pink Line’s planned opening, BJP MP Tejasvi Surya and Congress MLA Dinesh Gundu Rao disputed how much credit the Centre and Karnataka deserve for Bengaluru Metro. Surya cited the two governments’ committed contributions; Rao said Karnataka bears most of the project cost.

stories.headline: CHIEF MINISTER SET TO REVIEW BDA PROJECTS TODAY
paragraphs: Chief Minister D K Shivakumar is scheduled to review Bangalore Development Authority projects on Monday, focusing on traffic relief, urban development and long-pending housing issues. The Chief Minister’s Office said new initiatives and a computerised housing application system were expected to be discussed.

stories.headline: PINK LINE ELEVATED STRETCH LIKELY TO OPEN THIS FRIDAY
paragraphs: The 7.5-km elevated stretch of Namma Metro’s Pink Line, from Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere, is likely to be inaugurated on November 13, with passenger service expected the following day. The report noted that BMRCL had not formally confirmed the inauguration date.

stories.headline: CHENNAI OPEN SINGLES FINAL MOVED TO 11 AM TODAY
paragraphs: The WTA 250 Chennai Open women’s singles final between defending champion Janice Tjen and Magda Linette was postponed after rain and poor air quality disrupted Sunday’s play. Organisers rescheduled the match for 11 a.m. Monday; the same tickets remain valid.

stories.headline: PARTLY CLOUDY; NO WARNING FOR BENGALURU TODAY
paragraphs: The India Meteorological Department forecast partly cloudy skies in Bengaluru on Monday, with a minimum temperature of 20°C and a maximum of 29°C. No warning is in effect for the city.
